Project.name: media-analysis-platform
Project.annotation: GRACE requirements source of truth for the single-user channel-aware target media analysis product model.
Project.keywords: media_asset, stored_object, collection, inbox, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, analysis_run_step, artifact, diagnostic, channel_account, channel_surface, operation_request, telegram, web, mcp, postgres, minio, workers, copperasr

Purpose.purpose-1: Define the target product architecture for a single human user who can work through Telegram, Web, MCP, and future channels.
Purpose.purpose-2: Keep API-owned product state separate from channel presentation state and worker execution state.
Purpose.purpose-3: Give later Beads a stable requirements target for contracts, storage, orchestration, workers, Web, Telegram, MCP, diagnostics, retention, channel recovery, and evidence gates.

TargetArchitectureReset.bead: Defines the from-scratch target architecture, table set, API operation groups, DTO/type naming, app boundaries, user flows, migration stages, and verification matrix.
TargetArchitectureReset.rule: The product currently has one human user. Do not introduce owners, workspaces, workspace members, or team authorization until a real multi-user requirement exists.
Channel identity is modeled through channel_accounts and channel_surfaces; channels can store presentation and recovery state but cannot own product lifecycle.

The target vocabulary is media_asset, stored_object, collection, inbox, selection_snapshot, selection_snapshot_item, analysis_run, analysis_run_step, analysis_run_step_input, artifact, artifact_subject, diagnostic, channel_account, channel_surface, and operation_request.

The current local database is disposable for the target rebuild. Implementations may delete, recreate, truncate, or rebuild current schema/data and must not spend effort preserving or backfilling existing local rows unless a future production-data requirement is approved.

Removed implementation-era product names may appear only as historical deletion evidence or negative regression checks. Active contracts, code paths, user flows, and new documentation use the target vocabulary only.
If any older GRACE section conflicts with the target architecture document, the target architecture document wins until the corresponding migration packet rewrites the older section.

CanonicalVocabulary.term: A durable API-owned record for one user-provided material such as text, URL, file, photo, image, audio, voice, video, or document.
The API-owned stored bytes, external URI, text body, checksum, size, MIME type, and retention metadata behind a media_asset or artifact.
A durable channel-account-scoped grouping of media_asset references used for user organization and later analysis.
The default collection for each channel account where new media_asset records land unless the caller names another collection.
An immutable ordered snapshot of media_asset references, options, and access scope captured when a user decides what to analyze.
A user-facing run created from one selection_snapshot; it owns lifecycle, diagnostics, events, and artifact lineage.
An internal worker-claimable execution step with worker_kind, step_kind, lifecycle status, and cancellation/finalization state behind an analysis_run.
An internal execution input declaration that says which selection_snapshot_item or artifact a worker step may read.
A durable result or diagnostic object produced by analysis_run execution and resolved through API-governed access rules.
A lineage link from an artifact to the run, step, selection snapshot, selected item, media asset, or diagnostic it represents.

ModelChain.chain: media_asset -> collection/inbox -> immutable selection_snapshot -> analysis_run -> analysis_run_step/artifact -> artifact_subject lineage
ModelChain.rule: Adapters create and manage media_asset and collection state before execution; they do not expose transient submission modes as the product model.
analysis_run creation always references a selection snapshot, never mutable collection contents directly.
Later edits to the inbox or any collection never mutate an existing selection or analysis_run.

AccessScope.scope: All media_asset, collection, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, artifact, diagnostic, and retention decisions are scoped to a channel_account in the current single-user product.
Telegram chat/user, Web account/session, and MCP caller identities are resolved into channel_account/caller scope at the API boundary.
AccessScope.rule: Cross-channel-account reads, writes, selection reuse, run access, and artifact access are rejected before storage mutation.
Idempotency keys, pagination cursors, optimistic versions, and diagnostic queries are channel-account-scoped.
Public collection and paginated list envelopes always encode items as an array, including empty collections and empty pages.
No alternate caller-scope product entity exists in the target model; channel_account is the only access scope.

Requirement.Action: Create media_asset records from Telegram, Web, MCP, and server-side import callers through one API-owned ingestion boundary.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Supported inputs include text, URL, generic file, photo/image, audio/voice, and video/document; each accepted item records channel_account access scope, stored_object or origin metadata, content hash when available, size, MIME type, adapter origin, creation time, validation status, retention policy, and diagnostics pointer.

Requirement.Action: Maintain inbox and user collections independently of execution.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Every channel_account has a default inbox; callers can list, create, rename, archive, delete, and reorder collection items subject to channel-account scope and optimistic version checks. Accepted media appends to the next active collection position and must not create duplicate active positions in inbox or user collections.

Requirement.Action: Create immutable selection_snapshots from explicit ordered media_asset references.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Selection snapshot creation validates channel-account access, media availability, requested analysis options, ordering, duplicate policy, and size limits; the stored snapshot captures item ids, stored_object/origin metadata needed for execution, option values, creator, timestamps, and validation diagnostics.

Requirement.Action: Create analysis_run records only from selection_snapshots.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: analysis_run creation records selection_snapshot id, channel_account scope, run type, delivery preference, initial queued status, idempotency key, evidence-gate status, diagnostics channel, planned analysis_run_steps, and analysis_run_step_inputs. Execution rows stay internal and must not become the public product surface.

Requirement.Action: Plan prerequisite execution inside the API before workers run.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: For transcription runs, API maps selected materials to transcription steps so workers can produce one combined text artifact from original text materials, ready reusable transcript artifacts, and newly transcribed speech media. Ready channel_account-scoped transcript artifacts become explicit analysis_run_step_inputs, while only missing speech inputs remain selection_snapshot_item work for ASR. For report or deep_research runs, API requires ready transcript/text-corpus artifacts or creates prerequisite transcription steps first. If a prerequisite cannot be planned or satisfied, API records diagnostics with codes analysis_prerequisite_missing, analysis_prerequisite_failed, or analysis_prerequisite_unavailable and does not leave the user without visible status.

Requirement.Action: Run speech transcription through CopperASR as the only active ASR backend.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: For audio, voice, video, and URL speech sources, transcription workers call the dedicated CopperASR HTTP runtime through COPPER_ASR_* configuration, publish transcript_plain, transcript_segmented_markdown, transcript_docx, run_manifest, and run_diagnostics artifacts through the API, include sanitized provider metadata only in service artifacts, map provider failures to stable asr_* diagnostics, and keep Telegram, Web, and MCP provider-agnostic in normal user flows. Text-origin selection items are included directly in transcript artifacts and counted as included run_manifest items rather than skipped diagnostics; text-only selections produce transcript artifacts without invoking ASR. Legacy ASR imports, env switches, model cache volumes, dependencies, and fallback tests are removed from active runtime paths.

Requirement.Action: Reuse ready transcript artifacts for repeated media instead of sending already-transcribed speech through ASR again.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: For a channel_account-scoped single-source Telegram selection whose stored_object id or checksum already belongs to a terminal successful single-source transcription run with an available transcript artifact, the API exposes that reusable transcript and adapters deliver the existing artifact immediately without creating a new selection_snapshot or analysis_run. For mixed multi-item selections, API planning converts each reusable speech source into a transcript_artifact step input, keeps only missing speech sources as ASR selection_snapshot_item inputs, preserves text-origin inputs directly, and assembles final transcript/report inputs in selection_snapshot order. Artifacts from ambiguous multi-item transcription runs must not be reused as if they belonged to one unrelated source. Result_artifact_surface delivery deduplication remains restart-safe, but it must not block an explicit resend caused by a new duplicate user input.

Requirement.Action: Cancel analysis_run records through a cooperative API-owned lifecycle.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Canceling an unclaimed queued run terminally records canceled and stops queued tasks. Canceling a claimed run records cancel_requested, preserves the claimed task for worker observation, stops unclaimed queued tasks, exposes cancel_requested through worker cancel-check, and forces late worker finalization to resolve as canceled rather than succeeded or failed.

Requirement.Action: Expose artifacts as analysis_run outputs with API-governed preview and download metadata.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Artifacts include transcript, summary, report, extracted structured data, source manifest, execution log, and diagnostic bundles as applicable; each artifact records channel_account scope, run id, kind, content type, size, checksum, stored_object reference, visibility, retention state, preview metadata, and artifact_subject lineage where the artifact represents a selected item, step, prerequisite, or diagnostic.

Requirement.Action: Preserve rejected or partially processed records as diagnostics instead of silently dropping them.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Ingestion, selection, run, adapter, worker, artifact, cancellation, retention, and permission failures expose stable diagnostic codes, human-readable messages, provider or adapter context when safe, correlation ids, timestamps, and remediation hints.

Requirement.Action: Apply retention policies consistently across stored_objects, media_asset records, selection_snapshots, runs, artifacts, diagnostics, and deleted collection membership.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Retention rules define soft delete, hard delete eligibility, artifact expiry, stored object body expiry, export, and audit evidence preservation without orphaning run history.

Requirement.Action: Keep Telegram, Web, and MCP as thin adapters over the same API-owned state.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Adapters may shape presentation and local transport acknowledgements, but durable inbox, collection, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, artifact, retention, and diagnostics semantics are owned by the API. Telegram inbox rendering and actions follow collection membership rather than the broad media inventory. Telegram status copy and action labels are Russian-first and make collection actions plus run controls explicit to the user; successful processing results are delivered immediately as Telegram document messages and recorded as result_artifact_surface rows for duplicate prevention rather than relying on a Result button as the normal path. Web presents simple human wording and must not make internal names such as media_asset, selection_snapshot, analysis_run_step, channel_surface, opaque ids, run manifests, or diagnostic internals load-bearing UI terms outside explicit admin/debug views. MCP may expose technical target vocabulary because it is a tool contract context.

Requirement.Action: Run report and research analysis from prepared transcript or text-corpus artifacts.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: For audio, video, voice, or other speech media, transcription produces transcript artifacts before report or research execution. Agent-runner receives declared analysis_run_step_inputs for ready transcript or text-corpus artifacts plus safe metadata, materializes those artifacts as harness input, publishes report or research artifacts through analysis_run, and records or receives a prerequisite diagnostic instead of transcribing or processing raw speech media itself when required text input is missing.

Requirement.Action: Persist external interaction surfaces without coupling domain entities to consumer-specific UI.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Channel surfaces store channel_account-scoped channel, surface type, surface key, opaque address, address fingerprint, opaque display state, lifecycle status, version, and timestamps through an internal API. Subject links are stored separately with subject type, subject id, and subject role; event history is append-only. Domain tables must not gain Telegram-specific or consumer-specific message fields, and channel surface display state must not alter media_asset, collection, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, artifact, or diagnostic lifecycle.

When a channel reuses one active address for a different surface key, the internal channel_surface upsert must supersede the previous active surface before creating or updating the new active surface, so presentation rebinding cannot leak a database uniqueness failure to users.

DeletedArchitecture.rule: Former public routes and schemas centered on immediate transcription execution, grouped pre-run submission state, or public source-set terminology are deleted from the target product architecture.
Former batch toggles and draft semantics are not wrapped, aliased, or preserved as user-facing modes.
Backend execution rows and worker queue messages may remain as implementation details behind analysis_run, but product requirements must name analysis_run as the public run surface.
Historical implementation evidence may be kept only when clearly labeled as deleted architecture or internal execution proof; it must not define target user flows.

Telegram.rule: Telegram accepts messages, files, URLs, media groups, and inline commands as input capture and management gestures over the current materials/inbox collection.
Telegram round video messages delivered by the Bot API as video_note must be treated as video media inputs and enter the same upload, selection, and transcription path as regular Telegram videos.
Telegram shows the current inbox or collection status after accepted input and offers explicit actions to create a selection and run analysis.
Telegram callback payloads address API-owned media_asset, collection, selection_snapshot, and analysis_run identifiers with versions where mutation is allowed.

Telegram shows background active analysis_run state separately from the current material selection. The current selection can start a new processing run unless the card is focused on an active run. Cancel actions target either the focused active run or, when there is no focus, the latest visible active run by run id plus version.

Telegram active processing cards show user-facing material duration, current execution stage from analysis_run events, and elapsed processing time without exposing provider internals such as VAD/ASR timings or raw worker progress_stage values.

Telegram main-card diagnostics actions are scoped to the analysis_run launched from the current card focus; historical terminal runs do not create generic result actions for a new or unstarted inbox selection, and successful processing results are auto-delivered as files instead of becoming a normal Result-button workflow.

After a successful Telegram result file delivery, the adapter clears only the active inbox or collection membership through the API collection mutation path; immutable selection_snapshots, analysis_runs, artifacts, and diagnostics remain historical records.
Telegram may persist message mappings through the internal channel surfaces API, but the API treats those mappings as opaque channel surfaces rather than Telegram-specific domain fields.

After accepted Telegram input, a status refresh or channel_surface persistence failure must not turn the saved inbox mutation into a user-facing backend failure; the adapter confirms the saved material and offers /inbox recovery while logging the presentation-layer failure.

Compose-owned Telegram ingestion must use a local Telegram Bot API server for large media so aiogram getFile/download paths do not rely on the cloud Bot API file-size-limited download path. The local server requires TELEGRAM_API_ID and TELEGRAM_API_HASH credentials, stores data in a persistent telegram-bot-api-data volume, and shares that volume read-only with the adapter when aiogram local mode returns absolute file paths.

Telegram processing launch for one uploaded media item must query API-owned reusable transcript state by stored_object identity before creating a new run, and a matched transcript artifact is delivered as a fresh Telegram document response for the new user action when the processing result is a transcript.

Telegram mixed selections rely on API-owned analysis_run planning for partial transcript reuse; the adapter must not decide reusable transcript subsets from Telegram file identity or mutable inbox state.

Telegram current materials panels, active run cards, and delivered result messages are represented as current_materials_panel, analysis_task_surface, and result_artifact_surface channel_surfaces; restart recovery may restore or recreate those surfaces but must not use them to mutate product lifecycle.
Internal active channel_surface listing must honor subject_type and subject_id filters so current materials or task-card surfaces cannot be mistaken for delivered result artifact surfaces.
Telegram resolves chat/user scope to channel_account and uses target public calls for media_assets, collection membership, selection_snapshots, analysis_runs, artifacts, and diagnostics.
Repeated Telegram chat/user channel_account resolution must return the persisted channel_account row id from the API conflict path before media_asset create or upload requests reference that id.

Web.rule: Web is a simple human-facing management surface for browsing materials, creating groups, curating the current selection, launching analysis, and reviewing results, progress, errors, and downloads.

Web calls the target public API for media_assets, selection_snapshots, analysis_runs, artifacts, and diagnostics, but normal UI copy must avoid load-bearing internal terms such as media_asset, selection_snapshot, analysis_run_step, channel_surface, Run builder, Artifacts, Diagnostics, Run manifest, Analysis run, Media item, raw ids, and diagnostic internals outside explicit admin/debug views.

MCP.rule: MCP exposes target tool calls for create_media_asset, list_media_assets, search_media_assets, get_media_asset, delete_media_asset, get_inbox, create_collection, list_collections, get_collection, update_collection, update_collection_items, create_selection_snapshot, get_selection_snapshot, run_analysis, list_runs, get_run, cancel_run, retry_run, list_run_events, list_artifacts, get_artifact, get_artifact_preview, refresh_artifact, and get_diagnostics.

EvidenceGates.gate: Planning proof shows the target table set, API operations, DTO/type names, app boundaries, user flows, implementation stages, and test matrix are all covered by docs/architecture/single-user-channel-aware-target-architecture.md.

Contracts prove public vocabulary uses the target names media_asset, stored_object, collection/inbox, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, analysis_run_step_input, artifact, artifact_subject, diagnostic, channel_account where needed, and channel_surface only for internal channel runtime APIs.

Storage tests prove single-user/channel-account scope, channel identity boundaries, immutable selection snapshots, analysis_run_step_inputs, artifact_subject lineage, lifecycle transitions, idempotency, retention, diagnostics persistence, and channel surface recovery.
API tests prove adapters share the same state, prerequisite planning is visible through runs/diagnostics, and removed public product routes are absent from the target contract.

Worker tests prove execution consumes sealed snapshots and declared step inputs, agent-runner consumes ready transcript/text-corpus artifacts for report and research work, and results are reported through analysis_run artifacts and diagnostics.

ASR runtime tests and docs prove CopperASR is the only active transcription backend, provider metadata is service-scoped, legacy ASR paths are absent from active runtime surfaces, and failures resolve into stable diagnostics rather than generic unavailable errors.

Telegram, Web, and MCP tests prove management-first flows without user-facing batch toggles or immediate execution-only assumptions; Web tests also prove normal UI copy stays human and avoids internal technical vocabulary.
Compose or equivalent runtime proof verifies end-to-end ingestion, selection, run, artifact, diagnostics, and retention behavior.

The target coverage matrix maps every table, API operation, user flow, failure mode, deleted-surface rule, non-goal, app boundary, and data reset rule to implementation proof, automated proof, QA proof, or an explicit remaining Bead.

The coverage inventory reports native per-surface metrics where tools support them, records pass/fail-only probes separately, and fails if active target paths reintroduce removed public vocabulary or target reset migrations recreate removed tables.

NonGoals.item: Reintroducing old public product route vocabulary as an alias layer.
Preserving grouped pre-run submission state as the user-facing collection model.
